FIVE MONTREALERS 
TO BE HONORED BY 
SGWU ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 


SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS 
UNIVERSITY AND SCHOOLS 


METROPOLITAN YMCA 
OF MONTREAL 


May Ist, 1963 


FIVE MONTREALERS WILL BE HONORED FOR THEIR CITIZENSHIP AND 
SPECIAL SERVICE TO SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY BY THE 
ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI. IN ANNOUNCING THE HONORS, J. G. 
BRADLEY, AWARDS CHAIRMAN OF THE ALUMNI, STATED HE EXPECTS 
OVER 350 GRADUATES TO ATTEND THE SPECIAL CEREMONIES, MAY 
15TH, AT THE WINDSOR HOTEL WHEN THE ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 
WILL BESTOW HONORARY LIFE MEMBERSHIPS UPON THREE GOVERNORS 
OF THE UNIVERSITY AND TWO MEMBERS OF THE FACULTY. 


TO BE HONORED ARE JOHN B. FROSST, THE SENIOR MEMBER OF THE 
BOARD OF GOVERNORS, HAVING BEEN APPOINTED IN 19333 LT.-COL. 
S. C. HOLLAND, A GOVERNOR SINCE 19) AND J. H. ANDREWS, A 
GOVERNOR SINCE 1951. THE FACULTY TO BE HONORED ARE OR. J. W. 
BRIDGES, APPOINTED TO SIR GEORGE IN 190 AND FOR MANY YEARS 
CHAIRMAN OF THE DEPARTMENT OF PSYCHOLOGY; AND PROFESSOR 
DOUGLASS BURNS CLARKE WHO BEGAN TEACHING PART TIME AT SIR 
GEORGE WILLIAMS IN 1932, WAS APPOINTED REGISTRAR IN 196, 
AND VICE=-PRINCIPAL IN 1956. 


FORMALLY INSCRIBED SCROLLS WILL BE PRESENTED TO EACH OF THE 

FIVE NEW HONORARY LIFE MEMBERS. IN 25 YEARS ONLY FOUR PRE- 
VIOUS SUCH AWARDS HAVE BEEN MADE, THE LATE DR. K. E. NORRIS, 
PRINCIPAL, DR. H. F. HALL, PRINCIPAL EMERITUS, DR. B. W. 
ROBERTS, CHANCELLOR, AND DR. C. W. THOMPSON, PROFESSOR EMERITUS. 


HONORARY LIFE MEMBERSHIP 
SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY 
ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 
BIOGRAPHICAL NOTES: 


LT.-COL. S. C. HOLLAND 


Lieutenant-Colone! S. C. Holland, President and Managing 
Director of the Robert Mitchel! Co., became a member of 
the Board of Governors in the Spring of I9hh, although his 
contact with and service to the University predates this 
event. He was Officer Commanding the Artillery Regiment 
with which the Sir George Williams Military Training Unit 
was associated during the war. In 1945, Colonel Holland 
received the official acknowledgement of the-Governors for 
the contribution which he and his officers of the Second 
Anti-Aircraft Regiment R.C.A. had made to the University 


and its students. 


As an active member of the Board, Colone! Holland has con- 
tinued to show his interest in the University in many ways. 
For years, he has been the Governors! representative on the 
Athletic Council and has served as a member of the Executive 
Committee. He has also served as Honorary Commanding Officer 
of the Sir George Williams University Contingent of the 
C.0.T.C. As a leading Rotarian, as President of the Mental 
Health Association and in many other ways, he is an out- 


standing member of our community. 


HONORARY LIFE MEMBERSHIP 
SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY 
ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 
BIOGRAPHICAL NOTES: 


JOHN BURR FROSST, Ph. G. 


Mr. John B. Frosst is the senior member of the Board of 
Governors, having been appointed to the Board in 1933. 

Many good causes have benefited from his generosity and 

his leadership. Outstanding among these is the YMCA, 
local, national and international. Mr. Frosst's relation- 
ships with Sir George Williams University have been many. 
His leadership at certain critical times has been invaluable. 
He was chairman of the $3.5 million capital funds campaign 
in 1952 which made possible the construction of the present 
university building. He is the founder of the Charles E. 
Frosst Medal in memory of his distinguished father, which 


is awarded each year to the outstanding graduate in Commerce. 
J. HARMON ANDREWS 


Mr. Js Harmon Andrews may well be called a senior citizen 

of Montreal. In addition to a distinguished business career 

he has served the interests of many institutions with modesty, 
fidelity and generosity. Mr. Andrews became a member of the 
Board of Governors in 1951 and since that time has taken an 
active interest in the affairs of the University. On at least 
fwo occasions, he has shown his generous interest in good 
sportsmanship by presentations to outstanding University basket- 
ball teams. On his retirement, after fifty years' service at 
Lyman'ts Limited, he established the magnificent J. H. Andrews 
Limited Scholarship which is highly valued by faculty, students, 


and graduates at Sir George Williams University. 


HONORARY LIFE MEMBERSHIP 
SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY 
ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 
BIOGRAPHICAL NOTES: 


DR. J. W. BRIDGES 

Born in Prince Edward Island, he began his teaching career 
in a country school at the age of 18. Graduated from McGill 
in I91l with the Prince of Wales Gold Medal in Philosophy. 
He finished his M.A. in Psychology at Harvard in 1912 and a 


doctorate in I9I5. 


Dr. Bridges, a leading Canadian in his field, was three times 
a pioneer in the field of psychology in North America; he was 
the first student of psychology to receive a medical intern- 
ship. There are scores of them now al! over the continent. 
He interned at Boston Psychopathic Hospital in 1913. In 
192), he was appointed Professor in the Medical Faculty of 
McGill University and, as such, was the first psychologist to 
receive a professorship in a medical school. He is also the 
first Canadian-born psychologist to publish on the subject. 
First came "A Point Scale for Measuring Psychology" in I9Ith 


and later "Outline of Abnormal Psychology", 1919. 


Dr. Bridges is a Fellow of the American Association for the 
Advancement of Science. He has been nominated a Fellow and 
Life Member of the American Psychological Association, is a 
Fellow of the Canadian Psychological Association and was its 


Honorary President in 1959. 


Dr. Bridges is acknowledged for his development of Psychology 
at Sir George Williams University. His inspirational work 
with students at Sir George has encouraged over 100 young men 


and women to distinguish themselves in graduate studies over 


the years. 


HONORARY LIFE MEMBERSHIP 
SIR GEORGE WILLIAMS UNIVERSITY 
ASSOCIATION OF ALUMNI 
BIOGRAPHICAL NOTES: 


PROFESSOR DOUGLASS BURNS CLARKE, B.A., M.A. 


Professor Douglass Burns Clarke, M.A., was born in Montreal 
on Stanley Street in a house which formerly occupied the 
site of the present University building. His connection 
with Sir George Williams University was thereby preordained 


and a foregone conclusion. 


Professor Clarke graduated in the First University Graduating 
Class of Sir George Williams College. In 1932, Professor 
Clarke joined the teaching staff of Sir George Williams 
College as a part-time lecturer in Fine Arts, and accepted 

a full-time position in the College after his graduation in 
1936. In 193, he became the Acting Registrar, succeeding 
Dr. E. F. Sheffield. In 196, he was appointed Registrar 

and Professor of English and Fine Arts. In 1956, he was 


appointed Vice-Principal. 


Douglass Burns Clarke is an educator, a devotee of the theatre 
and arts, and a humanitarian. He participates in activities 
that reflect the breadth of his interests. In 196, he be- 

came the Secretary of the Psychological Association of the 
Province of Quebec until !950 when he became President. From 
1956 to 1958, he was the President of the Montreal Chapter of 
the Humanities Association of Canada. He has been active in 
numerous refugee and foreign student aid committees. Tirelessly, 
he gives his services on a variety of Committees of the Rotary 
Club of Montreal, as a member of the Board of Directors of the 


Meadville Conference of Unitarian Churches and as Secretary and 


later Vice-President of the Church of the Messiah in Montreal.
